extracted.intended_audience: Cornell faculty and researchers preparing NSF proposals (any career stage) seeking guidance on Broader Impacts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and writing the NSF Broader Impacts section of research proposals, including priorities, review criteria, design principles, partnership and budgeting advice, and evaluation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "the potential to benefit society and contribute to the achievement of specific, desired societal outcomes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core NSF definition. The page notes that researchers are generally confident describing intellectual merit but defining Broader Impacts can be challenging; Research Development (ReD) offers workshops, partnership connections, and grant writing support to help craft this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2025 NSF Broader Impact Priorities (statutory categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are advised to prioritize the first six categories listed in the 42 USC 1862p-14: Increasing the economic competitiveness of the United States; Advancing of the health and welfare of the American public; Supporting the national defense of the United States; Enhancing partnerships between academia and industry in the United States; Developing an American STEM workforce that is globally competitive through improved pre-kindergarten through grade 12 STEM education and teacher development, and improved undergraduate STEM education and instruction; Improving public scientific literacy and engagement with science and technology in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of June 18, 2025, these six categories are prioritized. The seventh category, “Expanding participation of women and individuals from underrepresented groups in STEM,” is deprioritized. Applicants should align Broader Impacts activities with these prioritized societal outcomes where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected characteristics guidance (engagement and non-preferencing)
rubrics_metrics.description: "NSF's broadening participation activities... must aim to create opportunities for all Americans everywhere. These efforts should not preference some groups at the expense of others, or directly/indirectly exclude individuals or groups. Research projects with more narrow impact limited to subgroups of people based on protected class or characteristics do not effectuate NSF priorities."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As of April 25, 2025, engagement activities based on protected characteristics may be conducted only as part of broad engagement activities; legally mandated NSF programs for protected groups continue to operate provided they do not preference or limit participation. See institutional legal guidance for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Review Criterion: Potential to benefit society
rubrics_metrics.description: What is the potential for the proposed activity to benefit society or advance desired societal outcomes?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe clear societal outcomes your activities aim to achieve and evidence that those outcomes are valuable and attainable. Tie outcomes to prioritized NSF categories when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Review Criterion: Creativity and transformative potential
rubrics_metrics.description: To what extent do the proposed activities suggest and explore creative, original or potentially transformative concepts?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize novel or original approaches to achieving Broader Impacts; however, innovation can also come from reimagining or scaling existing proven efforts rather than inventing wholly new programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Review Criterion: Quality of the plan and assessment mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the plan for carrying out the proposed activities well-reasoned, well-organized and based on sound rationale? Does the plan incorporate a mechanism to assess success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear, logical implementation plan with milestones, measurable goals, and mechanisms for evaluation and refinement. Use evidence or literature to justify chosen approaches and describe how success will be measured over time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Review Criterion: Qualifications of personnel and institution
rubrics_metrics.description: How well qualified is the individual, team or institution to conduct the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate relevant experience, expertise, and prior accomplishments of the PI and team. Include partnerships or outside experts where needed to fill gaps in capacity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broader Impacts Review Criterion: Adequacy of resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Are there adequate resources available to the principal investigator (either at the home institution or through collaborations) to carry out the proposed activities?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document available institutional support, collaborators, and realistic budgets. Showing committed resources and budgeted partner support increases credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Broader Impacts related to research
rubrics_metrics.description: Broader Impacts can be related to research, including: your research activities; activities directly related to your research; activities that are supported by, but complementary to, your research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify whether BI activities are integral to the research (e.g., research dissemination, translational partnerships), directly leverage research outputs, or are complementary educational/outreach efforts supported by the project budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct a credible impact identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify where your field intersects with societal needs, challenges, and opportunities. Which societal needs and issues most connect to your research? Which societal issues are most important to you, or the future of your field?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build on past experiences, genuine interests, and existing networks. Create a realistic 3–5 year plan that can launch toward larger goals. Structure proposals to connect research and education aims with societal needs and integrate these components into your plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be strategic (goals, prioritization, evidence base)
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand and articulate how your Broader Impacts plan advances NSF's vision. Think carefully about the goals of your plan, have short-term and long-term goals, and a pathway of resources, activities, and partners that connect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize efforts that can be tracked and measured. Broader Impacts should not be a list of unrelated outreach activities; root the plan in societal needs and use data/literature to demonstrate the need. Leverage existing campus/community resources rather than reinventing proven programs. Note NSF priority on broadening participation (subject to protected-characteristics guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate expertise (use best practices and evidence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build on best practices for the chosen activity area and reference the literature and NSF data to show relevance. Approach the BI plan like a scientific research problem with literature cited, research questions, methods, and a plan to share results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite education, outreach, or evaluation literature and NSF indicators as appropriate. Consider training, seed grants, or collaborations to strengthen expertise and credibility. Use external experts/partners to fill gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish meaningful partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage your network or local community partners (e.g., science museums, public media, public service or public health centers, youth programs, professional societies) to strengthen effectiveness and access to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nurture partnerships year-round, ensure partner expertise and needs align with project goals, and discuss capacity and expectations. Community-based partners can help broaden participation and may assist with program evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate adequate resources and budget for partners
rubrics_metrics.description: Most Broader Impacts plans require resources to have an impact. Allocating a realistic budget for broader impacts shows commitment and credibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget for partner time and contributions; discuss with partners how much support they need. A realistic and itemized BI budget strengthens the plan's plausibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate research, education, and Broader Impacts aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Include your trainees (undergraduate through postdoctoral) in the Broader Impacts plan and make a case for how their participation supports their professional development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show how BI activities create learning and career development opportunities for trainees and how those activities connect to the research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate impacts and share your success
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a plan to evaluate and refine your efforts and demonstrate impact over time. This is only possible with clear and measurable project goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop an evaluation plan using campus or external consultants as needed, collect measurable outcomes, and share successes and generalizable results with public and professional networks (coordinate with communications staff). Use evaluation findings to refine and scale activities.
